title: Matthew Brown uncovers Immaculate Constellation, tied to Lue Elizondo

tellings.quote: maybe the weirdest, most interesting thing. It was like I figured out Immaculate Constellation. Lou Alzando's name was tied to that program. And then Lou Alzando is testifying with Michael Shaenberger saying um you know I can't confirm or deny whether I was read in

plain: Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, uncovered a secret program called Immaculate Constellation, and Luis Elizondo, a former Pentagon official who went public about its UFO studies, had his name tied to it, says Michels, who adds that Elizondo, testifying beside the journalist Michael Shellenberger, would only say he could not confirm or deny whether he had been "read in," that is, briefed into it. The program is known from an unsigned report that Shellenberger delivered to Congress and that Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of a House Oversight hearing on 13 November 2024 as a Pentagon document; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, Brown later said he wrote it, and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report says the program was "established following the public disclosure of the AATIP/AAWSAP programs by Luis Elizondo in 2017," those being small Pentagon efforts that studied unexplained aerial reports, and that internal records "confirm the claims of Mr. Lue Elizondo" about them. So the report links Elizondo to the program as the disclosure that preceded it; whether he had any role inside it, it neither says nor rules out.

discussion.by: Immaculate Constellation report (anonymous, entered into the House Oversight hearing record, 13 November 2024)
discussion.text: An unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report ties Luis Elizondo to the program by its origin: it was "established following the public disclosure of the AATIP/AAWSAP programs by Luis Elizondo in 2017", and internal records "confirm the claims of Mr. Lue Elizondo regarding AATIP/AAWSAP's mission, activities, and findings". That his name was tied to the program in the sense of a role in it is Jesse Michels' reading; the report links him to it as the disclosure it followed.
